c.question: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a project from idea to production.
c.answer: Our support team was drowning in repetitive questions, so I proposed a retrieval-augmented assistant. I built the pipeline with FastAPI and pgvector, but early on it hallucinated about 18 percent of the time on a test set I wrote. c.question: How would you evaluate a RAG system?
c.answer: I'd separate retrieval from generation. For retrieval I'd build a labelled set of questions with the right source passages and track recall at k and MRR. I'd run it in CI so prompt or model changes can't silently regress, and add online feedback to catch what the offline set misses.

c.question: How would you decide whether to add a cache in front of an LLM endpoint?
c.answer: First I'd check how repetitive the traffic is, because a cache only pays off if the hit rate is decent. The trade-offs are staleness, correctness for personalised answers, and cost of invalidation. For us I used a short TTL keyed on a normalised prompt, added request coalescing to avoid stampedes, and kept personalised responses out of the cache. I'd measure hit rate and p95 before and after.
